title: Student Identity Disclosure
description: The student (EE1) shares their personal identity information (student id) with the Grades Portal Web App (P1) during the login and submission process. This act of sharing causes a threat because the portal can identify the student uniquely.

title: Sensitive Data Exposure
description: The student (EE1) shares sensitive personal data (work file, course, submission timestamp) with the Grades Portal Web App (P1). This act of sharing causes a threat because the portal can access and potentially misuse this sensitive information.

title: Data Processing for Identification
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) receives the student's data and processes it to identify the student. This action at the destination causes a threat because the portal can link the submitted data to the student's identity.

title: Data Storage and Retention
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) stores the student's data (work file, course, submission timestamp) and retains it. This action at the destination causes a threat because the portal can store and potentially retain sensitive personal data indefinitely.

title: Student Identity Disclosure
description: The portal exposes the student's unique identifier (student id) in the request payload to the assignment & grading service without any authentication or authorization check.
assumptions: The portal assumes the student id is a public identifier and that the service will accept it.

title: Course and File Reference Disclosure
description: The portal exposes the course identifier and file reference in the request payload to the assignment & grading service without any authentication or authorization check.
assumptions: The portal assumes the course and file reference are public identifiers and that the service will accept them.

title: Requesting Role Disclosure
description: The portal exposes the requesting role (e.g., 'student', 'teacher', 'admin') in the request payload to the assignment & grading service without any authentication or authorization check.
assumptions: The portal assumes the requesting role is a public identifier and that the service will accept it.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The assignment & grading service processes the submitted data (student id, course, file reference) without verifying the identity of the requester or the legitimacy of the course/file reference.
assumptions: The service assumes the data is valid and the requester is authorized to access the course and file.

title: Data Storage of Sensitive Information
description: The assignment & grading service stores the student's unique identifier and course information in a way that allows for potential re-identification of the student.
assumptions: The service stores the data in a format that does not inherently prevent re-identification.

title: Student Identification
description: The source element (P2) shares the student's unique identifier (id) with the data flow. This act of sharing causes the threat because the identifier is now exposed in transit, potentially allowing an attacker to link or identify the student across different systems.
assumptions: The student id is a unique identifier that can be used for identification purposes.

title: Data Linking via Metadata
description: The data flow (DF3) transmits the assignment file containing student id, course, and submission time. The threat arises at the data flow level because the transmission of this data (meta-data) allows an attacker to link or identify the student by their id, even if the id itself is not directly visible in the payload.
assumptions: The assignment file contains a student id field that is transmitted during the data flow.

title: Data Processing and Storage
description: The destination element (DS1) receives the assignment file and stores it. The threat arises at the destination because the recipient may process or store the data in a way that causes the student's id to be associated with the course or submission time, potentially creating a permanent record that links the student to the course.
assumptions: The assignment store (DS1) stores the data in a way that links the student id to the course or submission time.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: The teacher (EE3) shares their identity information with the Grades Portal Web App (P1) during the login process. This allows the portal to potentially identify the teacher and associate their data with their specific courses.
assumptions: The login process requires the teacher to authenticate and provide their credentials.

title: Data Processing for Identification
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) receives the teacher's identity information and uses it to identify the teacher and associate their data with their specific courses for processing.
assumptions: The portal processes the submitted data to retrieve the queue of submissions.

title: Student Identity Disclosure
description: The portal shares student names and work content with the teacher, which may allow the teacher to identify specific students and access their private work.
assumptions: The teacher has access to the portal and the data is not encrypted or pseudonymized.

title: Student Work Content Exposure
description: The portal shares student work content with the teacher, which may allow the teacher to view or modify the student's private work.
assumptions: The teacher has access to the portal and the data is not encrypted or pseudonymized.

title: Teacher Identity Disclosure
description: Teacher (EE3) shares their identity (name, email, or other identifiers) with the Grades Portal Web App (P1) when recording a grade. This allows the portal to potentially link or identify the teacher, which may be sensitive information.

title: Student Identity Disclosure
description: Teacher (EE3) shares the student's unique identifier (student id) with the Grades Portal Web App (P1) when recording a grade. This allows the portal to potentially identify the student, which may be sensitive information.

title: Grader Identity Disclosure
description: Teacher (EE3) shares the grader's unique identifier (grader id) with the Grades Portal Web App (P1) when recording a grade. This allows the portal to potentially identify the grader, which may be sensitive information.

title: Data Linking Threat
description: The data flow (DF6) transmits teacher, student, and grader identifiers in transit. The meta-data about the parties (e.g., 'Teacher: EE3', 'Student: ID123', 'Grader: ID456') can be used to link or identify the individuals, even if the individual identities are not explicitly sent.

title: Data Processing Threat
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) receives the grade data and may process or store it in a way that causes a threat. For example, if the portal stores the teacher's name or email in a database, it creates a persistent record linking the teacher to the grade, which could be used for future identification.

title: Student ID Disclosure
description: The source element (Process P2) shares the student ID with the destination element (DataStore DS2) without any authentication or encryption. This allows the destination to potentially identify the student.
assumptions: The process does not use any authentication mechanism to verify the student's identity before sharing their ID.

title: Course Information Disclosure
description: The source element (Process P2) shares the course name with the destination element (DataStore DS2) without any authentication or encryption. This allows the destination to potentially identify the course.
assumptions: The process does not use any authentication mechanism to verify the course's existence or relevance before sharing its name.

title: Feedback Data Disclosure
description: The source element (Process P2) shares the feedback text with the destination element (DataStore DS2) without any authentication or encryption. This allows the destination to potentially identify the student or grader.
assumptions: The process does not use any authentication mechanism to verify the feedback's content or relevance before sharing it.

title: Grader ID Disclosure
description: The source element (Process P2) shares the grader ID with the destination element (DataStore DS2) without any authentication or encryption. This allows the destination to potentially identify the grader.
assumptions: The process does not use any authentication mechanism to verify the grader's identity before sharing their ID.

title: Timestamp Disclosure
description: The source element (Process P2) shares the timestamp with the destination element (DataStore DS2) without any authentication or encryption. This allows the destination to potentially identify the time of the grade.
assumptions: The process does not use any authentication mechanism to verify the timestamp's accuracy or relevance before sharing it.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: The student (EE1) shares their personal identity information with the Grades Portal Web App (P1) to request grades and feedback.

title: Data Processing for Personalization
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) receives the student's identity and uses it to personalize the feedback and grades, potentially linking the student to other data sources.

title: Student Identity Disclosure
description: The portal shares the student's unique identifier (e.g., student ID or email) with the external entity (Student) without explicit consent or a clear, opt-in mechanism for the student to control this sharing.

title: Teacher Feedback Data Leakage
description: The portal shares teacher feedback data (which may contain sensitive information about the student's academic performance or behavior) with the external entity (Student) without proper data minimization or consent.

title: Data Processing and Storage Risk
description: Upon receipt, the Student entity may process or store the shared data in a way that creates a profile or linkage that compromises the student's privacy, potentially leading to re-identification or misuse of their personal information.

title: Identity Confusion
description: The parent entity (EE2) shares its identity with the child entity (EE1) without explicit authentication or authorization. This allows the child to potentially impersonate the parent or access data associated with the parent's identity.
assumptions: The parent account is linked to the child account, but this linkage is not explicitly secured.

title: Data Processing Disclosure
description: The process (P1) processes the parent's identity information (EE2) and the child's identity information (EE1) to generate grades. This processing step may reveal sensitive identity data to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: The process does not have sufficient controls to mask or encrypt the identity data before processing.

title: Grade Data Exposure
description: The portal element (P1) shares the child's grade data with the parent (EE2) without any authentication or authorization checks. This allows the parent to access sensitive personal information.
assumptions: The portal is configured to display grades to any external entity.

title: Feedback Data Exposure
description: The portal element (P1) shares feedback data with the parent (EE2) without any authentication or authorization checks. This allows the parent to access sensitive personal information.
assumptions: The portal is configured to display feedback to any external entity.

title: Submission History Exposure
description: The portal element (P1) shares the child's submission history with the parent (EE2) without any authentication or authorization checks. This allows the parent to access sensitive personal information.
assumptions: The portal is configured to display submission history to any external entity.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The parent (EE2) receives the grades, feedback, and submission history and stores/processes them in a way that causes a privacy threat. The parent may use this data for its own purposes without the child's consent.
assumptions: The parent has no explicit consent to receive and process this specific data.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: The external entity (EE4) shares personal identifiers (e.g., email, name) with the Grades Portal Web App (P1) to create, modify, and disable accounts. This act of sharing causes the threat because the portal receives and stores this data, potentially allowing the portal to identify or link users to their accounts.
assumptions: The external entity has the authority to share this data.

title: Data Processing and Storage
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) receives the account data (names, emails, roles) from the external entity. The threat arises at the destination because the portal processes and stores this sensitive personal information, which may be used for internal purposes or shared with third parties without adequate safeguards.
assumptions: The portal has the capability to store and process this data.

title: Data Leakage
description: The source element (Process P2) shares account records and parent-child relationship links with the Account Directory (DataStore DS3). This act of sharing causes the threat because the data is exposed to unauthorized access or processing without proper authorization controls.

title: Unauthorized Processing
description: The destination element (DataStore DS3) receives the account records and parent-child relationship links. The threat arises because the recipient may store, process, or use this data in ways that cause privacy violations, such as linking records to personal identifiers or storing sensitive relationship data.

title: Data Leakage
description: The source element (Process P2) shares full grade records, assignments, and account directory with the external Cloud Hosting Provider (EE5) without any encryption or access controls. This act of sharing causes the threat because the data is exposed to an untrusted third party.
assumptions: The process does not use encryption for data in transit or at rest.

title: Data In Transit
description: The data-centric threat arises at the data flow (DF14) itself. The full grade records, assignments, and account directory are transmitted over the network in a format that could be intercepted or analyzed by the external Cloud Hosting Provider (EE5).
assumptions: The data is transmitted in plaintext or with weak encryption.

title: Unauthorized Processing
description: The destination element (Cloud Hosting Provider EE5) receives the data and processes or stores it in a way that causes the threat. The provider may store the sensitive grade records, assignments, and account directory without proper access controls, potentially leading to data breaches.
assumptions: The provider does not implement strict access controls or data minimization.

title: Grade Records Access
description: The source element (DataStore DS2) shares grade records with the Assignment & Grading Service (Process P2). This act of sharing causes the threat because the destination element (P2) may process or store the data in a way that causes the threat.

title: Grade Records Processing
description: The destination element (Process P2) receives the grade records and processes them to build student, parent, and teacher views. This processing may cause the threat if the views are used to identify or link individuals inappropriately.
